facts.value: The critical importance of the feet and legs is summed up by the traditional adage, 'no foot, no horse'.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: On average, a horse weighs 500 kilograms (1,100 lb).
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: The horse hoof begins with the distal phalanges, the equivalent of the human fingertip or tip of the toe, surrounded by cartilage and other specialized, blood-rich soft tissues such as the laminae.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: The exterior hoof wall and horn of the sole is made of keratin, the same material as a human fingernail.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: The hoof continually grows, and in most domesticated horses needs to be trimmed (and horseshoes reset, if used) every five to eight weeks.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: The hooves of horses in the wild wear down and regrow at a rate suitable for their terrain.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Some horses have horseshoes placed on their feet by a professional farrier for the protection of the hoof under certain conditions.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science
